old: *Kr.e.* (\"before Christ\") and *Kr.u.* (\"after Christ\") always come BEFORE the number, just like English BC/AD — this is an exception to Hungarian word order, where time expressions usually go before the noun, but here the abbreviation and the number form a fixed unit together: *Kr.e. 9-ben* (\"in 9 BC\"), not *a 9. Kr.e.-ben*.
new: *Kr.e.* (\"before Christ\") and *Kr.u.* (\"after Christ\") both come BEFORE the year in Hungarian: *Kr.e. 9-ben* (\"in 9 BC\"), *Kr.u. 9-ben* (\"in AD 9\"). English puts AD before the year but BC after it, so *Kr.e.* is the one to watch.
why: false comparison: 'just like English BC/AD' (BC follows the year in English); the claim of an exception to Hungarian word order is wrong
